title: Idempotent external ingestion stores the dedup set and the watermark in document state, not in worker memory
content:
The `external-feed-ingest` recipe states its thesis as one line: **the document is the checkpoint store.** Both the dedup set and the high-watermark live in document state, and the worker rebuilds them from state at startup via `seedFromState()`. An in-memory-only checkpoint is the bug the recipe exists to prevent — crash the worker mid-stream and it re-ingests everything since the last flush.

The subtler half is *which* value is the dedup key. It is `(source, externalId)`, **not** the watermark:

> The watermark is only a fetch optimization ("don't re-read the whole feed"). It is not the dedup mechanism, because real feeds redeliver: the same `externalId` can reappear at a *later* cursor, sailing straight past a watermark filter.

So the two do different jobs. The watermark tracks the feed's monotonic *delivery cursor* and bounds how much you re-read; the id-set answers the authoritative question "have I already recorded this?" On restart the id-set is what saves you.

The state schema keeps both in the document:

```graphql
type FeedLedgerState {
  source: String!
  watermark: Int!
  entries: [LedgerEntry!]!
}
```

Watermark advancement is folded into the domain operations (`max(watermark, sequence)`, so an out-of-order delivery cannot regress it) rather than living in a separate `setWatermark` op. And the reducer enforces uniqueness too, throwing `DuplicateEntry` — defence in depth against racing redeliveries that both pass the worker's in-memory check.

Corrections are modelled as explicit operations, never mutations: `markSuperseded` flips the old entry's status, sets `supersededBy`, and appends the corrected value as a *new* `RECORDED` entry. The original payload is never touched.

The same pattern appears in `inbound-webhook-bridge` for the push direction, where provider `event.id` values accumulate in the document's `processedEventIds`. Notably the recipe argues the crash-safety property is independent of where the loop lives — a long-running script or an `IProcessor` both work, because the guarantee comes from seeding state from the document.

Provenance: academy `05-Lookup/00-Cookbook.md`, External Feed Ingest recipe ("The one idea worth taking away", "Why externalId is the dedup key"), academy 6.2.2-dev.45.
description: Seeding the dedup id-set from document state at startup makes a worker restart a no-op; an in-memory-only checkpoint re-ingests everything since the last flush.
